The '''easystats''' collection of [[Open-source software|open source]] [[R packages]] was created in 2019 and primarily includes tools dedicated to the post-processing of statistical models.<ref name="easystats_birthday_blogpost">{{cite web |title=easystats: one year already. What's next? |url=https://www.r-bloggers.com/2020/01/easystats-one-year-already-whats-next/ |website=r-bloggers |access-date=14 January 2022 |date=23 January 2020}}</ref><ref name="easystats_github">{{cite web |title=easystats |url=https://github.com/easystats/easystats |website=GitHub |access-date=14 January 2022 |date=14 January 2022}}</ref> As of May 2022, the 10 packages composing the easystats ecosystem have been downloaded more than 8 million times, and have been used in more than 1000 scientific publications.<ref>{{cite web |title=easystats Downloads |url=https://github.com/easystats/easystats#downloads |website=GitHub |access-date=14 January 2022 |date=14 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Project "easystats" |url=https://www.researchgate.net/project/Project-easystats-making-statistical-computations-with-R-easier |website=ResearchGate |access-date=16 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Dominique Makowski's Google Scholar Profile |url=https://scholar.google.fr/citations?user=bg0BZ-QAAAAJ&hl=en |website=scholar.google.fr}}</ref> The ecosystem is the topic of several statistical courses, video tutorials and books.<ref>{{cite web |title=easystats: Quickly investigate model performance |url=https://www.business-science.io/r/2021/07/13/easystats-performance-check-model.html |website=Business Science |access-date=17 January 2022 |language=en |date=13 July 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Automate Textual Reports of Statistical Models in R! report / easystats |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_ypkrGyqyZ4 |website=YouTube | date=29 November 2021 |access-date=17 January 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Field |first1=Andy P. |title=Discovering statistics using R |date=2012 |location=Thousand Oaks, California |isbn=978-1446200469}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Analyse des corrélations avec easystats |url=https://rzine.fr/docs/20200526_glecampion_initiation_aux_correlations/index.html |website=rzine.fr |access-date=17 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Kennedy |first1=Ryan |title=Introduction to R for social scientists a Tidy programming approach |date=2021 |location=Boca Raton |isbn=9781000353877}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Monkman |first1=Martin |title=Data Science with R: A Resource Compendium |url=https://bookdown.org/martin_monkman/DataScienceResources_book/ |access-date=18 May 2022}}</ref>

The aim of easystats is to provide a unifying and consistent framework to understand and report statistical results. It is also compatible with other collections of packages, such as the [[tidyverse]]. Notable design characteristics include its [[API]], with a particular attention given to the names of functions and arguments (e.g., avoiding acronyms and abbreviations), and its low number of dependencies.<ref name="easystats_github"></ref>{{Better source needed|reason=Needs an [[WP:IS|independent source]]. We can't rely on the authors of the package to tell us what it's notable for.|date=June 2022}}

==History==
In 2019, [[Dominique Makowski]] contacted software developer Daniel Lüdecke with the idea to collaborate around a collection of R packages aiming at facilitating data science for users without a statistical or computer science background. The first package of '''easystats''', ''insight'' was created in 2019, and was envisioned as the foundation of the ecosystem.<ref name="easystats_birthday_blogpost"></ref> The second package that emerged, ''bayestestR'', benefitted from the joining of Bayesian expert Mattan S. Ben-Shachar. Other maintainers include Indrajeet Patil, Brenton M. Wiernik, Etienne Bacher, and Rémi Thériault.<ref>{{cite web |title=easystats Authors |url=https://easystats.github.io/easystats/authors.html |website=GitHub |access-date=11 November 2024 |date=11 November 2024}}</ref>

The '''easystats''' collection of packages as a whole received the 2023 Award from the [[Society_for_the_Improvement_of_Psychological_Science|Society for the Improvement of Psychological Science (SIPS)]].<ref>{{cite web |title=SIPS 2023 Awards Announced! |url=https://improvingpsych.org/2023/08/22/sips-2023-awards-announced/ |website=improvingpsych |access-date=29 September 2023 |date=22 August 2023}}</ref>

==Packages==
The '''easystats''' ecosystem contains ten semi-independent packages.
* ''insight'': This package serves as the foundation of the ecosystem as it allows manipulating objects from different [[R packages]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lüdecke |first1=Daniel |last2=Waggoner |first2=Philip D. |last3=Makowski |first3=Dominique |title=insight: A Unified Interface to Access Information from Model Objects in R |journal=Journal of Open Source Software |date=25 June 2019 |volume=4 |issue=38 |pages=1412 |doi=10.21105/joss.01412 |bibcode=2019JOSS....4.1412L |s2cid=198640623 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* ''datawizard'': This package implements some core data manipulation features.<ref name="datawizard">{{cite journal |last1=Patil |first1=Indrajeet |last2=Makowski |first2=Dominique |last3=Ben-Shachar |first3=Mattan S. |last4=Wiernik |first4=Brenton M. |last5=Bacher |first5=Etienne |last6=Lüdecke |first6=Daniel |title=datawizard: An R Package for Easy Data Preparation and Statistical Transformations |journal=Journal of Open Source Software |date=9 October 2022 |volume=7 |issue=78 |pages=4684 |doi=10.21105/joss.04684  |doi-access=free|bibcode=2022JOSS....7.4684P |url=https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.04684.pdf |access-date=29 September 2023}}</ref>
* ''bayestestR'': This package provides utilities to work with [[Bayesian statistics]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Makowski |first1=Dominique |last2=Ben-Shachar |first2=Mattan |last3=Lüdecke |first3=Daniel |title=bayestestR: Describing Effects and their Uncertainty, Existence and Significance within the Bayesian Framework |journal=Journal of Open Source Software |date=13 August 2019 |volume=4 |issue=40 |pages=1541 |doi=10.21105/joss.01541|bibcode=2019JOSS....4.1541M |s2cid=201882316 |doi-access=free }}</ref> The package received a Commendation award by the [[Society_for_the_Improvement_of_Psychological_Science|Society for the Improvement of Psychological Science (SIPS)]] in 2020.<ref>{{cite web |title=SIPS Awards |date=24 July 2018 |url=https://improvingpsych.org/mission/awards/ |access-date=21 August 2022}}</ref>
* ''correlation'': This package is dedicated to running [[correlation]] analyses.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Makowski |first1=Dominique |last2=Ben-Shachar |first2=Mattan |last3=Patil |first3=Indrajeet |last4=Lüdecke |first4=Daniel |title=Methods and Algorithms for Correlation Analysis in R |journal=Journal of Open Source Software |date=16 July 2020 |volume=5 |issue=51 |pages=2306 |doi=10.21105/joss.02306|bibcode=2020JOSS....5.2306M |s2cid=225530918 |doi-access=free |hdl=21.11116/0000-0013-3488-7 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
* ''performance'': This package allows the extraction of metrics of model performance.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lüdecke |first1=Daniel |last2=Ben-Shachar |first2=Mattan |last3=Patil |first3=Indrajeet |last4=Waggoner |first4=Philip |last5=Makowski |first5=Dominique |title=performance: An R Package for Assessment, Comparison and Testing of Statistical Models |journal=Journal of Open Source Software |date=21 April 2021 |volume=6 |issue=60 |pages=3139 |doi=10.21105/joss.03139|bibcode=2021JOSS....6.3139L |s2cid=233378359 |doi-access=free |hdl=21.11116/0000-0008-6A26-7 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
* ''effectsize'': This packages computes indices of effect size and standardized parameters.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ben-Shachar |first1=Mattan |last2=Lüdecke |first2=Daniel |last3=Makowski |first3=Dominique |title=effectsize: Estimation of Effect Size Indices and Standardized Parameters |journal=Journal of Open Source Software |date=23 December 2020 |volume=5 |issue=56 |pages=2815 |doi=10.21105/joss.02815|bibcode=2020JOSS....5.2815B |s2cid=229576898 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* ''parameters'': This package centres around the analysis of the parameters of a statistical model.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lüdecke |first1=Daniel |last2=Ben-Shachar |first2=Mattan |last3=Patil |first3=Indrajeet |last4=Makowski |first4=Dominique |title=Extracting, Computing and Exploring the Parameters of Statistical Models using R |journal=Journal of Open Source Software |date=9 September 2020 |volume=5 |issue=53 |pages=2445 |doi=10.21105/joss.02445|bibcode=2020JOSS....5.2445L |s2cid=225319884 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* ''modelbased'': This package computes model-based predictions, group averages and contrasts.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Makowski |first1=Dominique |last2=Ben-Shachar |first2=Mattan S. |last3=Wiernik |first3=Brenton M. |last4=Patil |first4=Indrajeet |last5=Thériault |first5=Rémi |last6=Lüdecke |first6=Daniel |title=modelbased: An R package to make the most out of your statistical models through marginal means, marginal effects, and model predictions |journal=Journal of Open Source Software |date=30 May 2025 |volume=10 |issue=109 |pages=7969 |doi=10.21105/joss.07969 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
* ''see'': This package interfaces with [[ggplot2]] to create visual plots.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lüdecke |first1=Daniel |last2=Patil |first2=Indrajeet |last3=Ben-Shachar |first3=Mattan S. |last4=Wiernik |first4=Brenton M. |last5=Waggoner |first5=Philip |last6=Makowski |first6=Dominique |title=see: An R Package for Visualizing Statistical Models |journal=Journal of Open Source Software |date=6 August 2021 |volume=6 |issue=64 |pages=3393 |doi=10.21105/joss.03393|bibcode=2021JOSS....6.3393L |s2cid=238778250 |doi-access=free |hdl=21.11116/0000-0008-FE71-B |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
* ''report'': This package implements an automated reporting of statistical models.
